finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker can provide a filename that includes shell metacharacters or a path traversal sequence.
finding.assumptions: The filename is directly passed to fopen without any validation or sanitization.

parsed.change_summary: No changes were made to the code as the reported finding (CWE-78: OS Command Injection) does not apply to the given code fragment. The function `load_ssh_private_key` does not execute any shell commands; it only opens a file using `fopen` with a filename parameter. There is no indication of shell metacharacter injection or command execution in the provided code.
parsed.how_trigger_is_blocked: The trigger described in the finding (an attacker providing a filename that includes shell metacharacters or a path traversal sequence) does not apply to the given code fragment. The function `load_ssh_private_key` does not execute any shell commands; it only opens a file using `fopen` with a filename parameter. There is no indication of shell metacharacter injection or command execution in the provided code.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the sink is fopen, which does not invoke a shell; therefore no command injection is possible. The source is a filename string, but passing it to fopen only opens a file, not a command. Path traversal or shell metacharacters in the filename do not lead to command execution. No check is needed for command injection. The reported trigger is therefore invalid.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker can provide a filename that includes shell metacharacters or a path traversal sequence.
finding.assumptions: The filename is directly passed to gcry_sexp_new without any validation or sanitization.

parsed.change_summary: No changes were made to the code as the reported finding does not apply to the given code fragment. The function `load_ssh_private_key` does not execute any OS commands or shell operations that could be vulnerable to OS Command Injection.
parsed.how_trigger_is_blocked: The trigger described in the finding no longer works because the code does not execute any OS commands or shell operations. The function only reads the content of a file and processes it using the `gcry_sexp_new` function from the Gcrypt library.

parsed.refutation_attempt: 1) Verified that the only use of the untrusted source "filename" is to open a file with fopen; no command string is constructed or passed to a shell. 2) Confirmed that the sink gcry_sexp_new merely parses the file contents into an s‑expression; it does not invoke any system or exec family calls. 3) No other checks or sanitisation on the filename influence any command execution path. 4) The code contains no constant arguments that could mask a command injection. 5) The path from filename to the sink is fully neutralised by the fact that the filename is only used for file I/O, not command execution. Therefore the OS Command Injection claim is unfounded.
